# Mixed growth preference controls and original-document guard

Eight independent XML controls are generated by
`tools/mixed_growth_preference_fixture.py` using the project's original
mixed-cell-width-content OPC shell. They vary 0/48-twip margins, CCC/CCCCC in
one automatic column versus C in the other, and an automatic/6000-twip merged
footer preference. The table preference stays 6000 twips. Body text and all
source assets are original project controls, without corpus XML or third-party
font binaries. Fixed ZIP metadata makes regeneration deterministic.

`tools/record_mixed_growth_preference.ps1` opens the exact source read-only in
the reference application, repaginates, records row-3 Cell.Width values, and
closes its own reference application instance. It does not export a PDF. These rounded logical
widths are not a claim of exact painted boundaries. Hashes bind the source and
case manifest. All eight controls remain diagnostic; no allocation correction
is claimed by adding them.

`corpus-reference.json` separately records 26 native monthly-header origins on
page 14 of local corpus #64, the business plan. It binds the original DOCX and
retained native reference PDF by SHA-256; neither source is redistributed. The
browser guard reads `DOCX_CORPUS_ROOT` (or this machine's corpus directory) and
skips when absent. It compares all 26 positions within the existing 0.2pt
geometry criterion and checks that the document still has 18 body pages.

This guard rejects a fractional-growth candidate that passed the independent
mixed-width and zero-inset controls: original page-14 maximum changed-origin
error increased from 0.12pt to 0.24pt. Of 289 matched changed text fragments,
169 worsened. Seventeen other page PNGs were identical; only the page-14 table
region differed. The candidate was not installed in production, and existing
expected failures were not removed.

OOXML references: ECMA-376 Part 1 17.4.29, 17.4.49, 17.4.63, 17.4.71 and
17.18.87. The allocation guidance allows algorithm flexibility. These native
observations establish no normative contradiction or document-specific rule.
